about: Official payment and contact facts for a small set of US payees. Every fact was read on the organisation's own website on the date in `checked`, and carries the page URL plus a short verbatim quote. Anything that could not be fetched and confirmed was left out. This is a demo registry, not a complete directory.
method_vocabulary_note: `gift_card` covers gift cards and prepaid/reloadable cards (for example MoneyPak or Green Dot). `payment_app` covers apps such as Venmo, Cash App and PayPal; `zelle` is listed separately. `bank_transfer` means paying from a checking or savings account. `card` means a credit or debit card.

official_domains.quote: Odd or misspelled web links can take you to harmful sites instead of IRS.gov.

phones.label: Help line for individuals
phones.quote: Individuals 800-829-1040 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time

accepted_methods.summary: Federal taxes can be paid from a bank account or by debit or credit card.
accepted_methods.quote: Pay your federal taxes by bank account, debit or credit card, digital wallet and more.

accepted_methods.summary: Checks and money orders are made payable to the U.S. Treasury.
accepted_methods.quote: Make the check, money order or cashier’s check payable to “U.S. Treasury” with the amount in dollars and cents.

never_methods.summary: The IRS never asks for or accepts gift cards for a tax bill.
never_methods.quote: the IRS never asks for or accepts gift cards as payment for a tax bill

never_methods.summary: The IRS says it will never call to demand immediate payment by gift card, prepaid debit card or wire transfer.
never_methods.quote: Call to demand immediate payment using a specific payment method such as a gift card, prepaid debit card or wire transfer.

contact_facts.summary: The IRS normally makes first contact by postal mail.
contact_facts.quote: We normally contact you the first time by mail delivered by the U.S. Postal Service.

contact_facts.summary: The IRS sends text messages only to people who opted in.
contact_facts.quote: We send text messages only when you opt in.

contact_facts.summary: The IRS sends email only to people who opted in.
contact_facts.quote: We email only when you opt in.

contact_facts.summary: The IRS says it will never threaten to have someone arrested for not paying.
contact_facts.quote: Threaten to bring in local police, immigration officers or other law enforcement to have the taxpayer arrested for not paying.

official_domains.quote: Our website, www.ssa.gov, is the best way to get help.

phones.label: National 800 number
phones.quote: You can call us at 1-800-772-1213 between 8:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m. local time, Monday through Friday.

never_methods.summary: Social Security says it will never require payment by cash, gift card, prepaid debit card, internet currency or wire transfer.
never_methods.quote: Require payment by cash, gift card, pre-paid debit card, internet currency, or wire transfer.

contact_facts.summary: Social Security says it will never demand immediate payment.
contact_facts.quote: Demand immediate payment from you.

contact_facts.summary: If there is a problem with a Social Security number or record, the agency typically mails a letter.
contact_facts.quote: If there is a problem with your Social Security number or record, we will typically mail you a letter.

contact_facts.summary: Social Security does not ask for sensitive information by social media, email or text message.
contact_facts.quote: Social Security will never ask for sensitive or personal information through social media, email, or text message.

payees.name: Medicare
aliases: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services

official_domains.quote: Create a secure Medicare.gov account to view your Original Medicare claims as soon as they’re processed to help spot mistakes sooner.

addresses.label: Premium payments by mail
addresses.address: Medicare Premium Collection Center, PO Box 790355, St. Louis, MO 63179-0355
addresses.quote: Medicare Premium Collection Center PO Box 790355 St. Louis, MO 63179-0355

accepted_methods.summary: Premiums can be paid online through a Medicare account by credit or debit card, HSA card, or checking or savings account.
accepted_methods.quote: Choose your payment method, like credit/debit card, Health Savings Account (HSA) card, or checking or savings account

accepted_methods.summary: Premiums can be paid by mail with a check, money order, credit card, debit card or HSA card.
accepted_methods.quote: Pay by check, money order, credit card, debit card, or Health Savings Account (HSA) card.

contact_facts.summary: Medicare says it will never call to sell anything or visit a home.
contact_facts.quote: Remember that Medicare will never call you to sell you anything or visit you at your home.

contact_facts.summary: If a caller asks for money or threatens to cancel benefits, Medicare says to hang up and call 1-800-MEDICARE.
contact_facts.quote: If someone calls and asks for your information, for money, or threatens to cancel your health benefits, hang up and call us 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227).

contact_facts.summary: Online premium payments should go only through the person's own Medicare account.
contact_facts.quote: Use only your Medicare account to pay your premiums.

official_domains.quote: visit USPS.com from your mobile device or computer for tracking and additional resources
To report USPS related smishing, send an email to spam@uspis.gov

contact_facts.summary: USPS does not send texts or emails about a package unless the customer first asked for tracking with a tracking number.
contact_facts.quote: USPS will not send customers text messages or e-mails without a customer first requesting the service with a tracking number

contact_facts.summary: USPS does not charge for its package tracking tools.
contact_facts.quote: USPS does not charge for these services!

contact_facts.summary: The FTC never asks people for money.
contact_facts.quote: The FTC will never ask you for money, threaten to arrest you, or promise you a prize.
